messages.subject: PLS graphing help
parts:
Hi all,

   I am doing a two.b.pls where one block is shape and the other block is ecological data and my points are species. I would like to present the warp grids for each end of the shape axis if possible and I have tried a variety of very basic methods to do so and none have worked for me. I would also be interested in labelling each species point and being able to see the x and y scores for each species point as I'm especially interested in the combinations of my ecological variables that are positively versus negatively loading along the second block axis. Here again, I've played around with a variety of basic functions to try to accomplish these things to no avail. Any suggestions would be most appreciated!

Thanks!

Jessica

messages.author: 60876d83c466f9b2
messages.subject: SV: [geomorph-r-package] PLS graphing help
parts:
Hey Jessica,


To visualize shape change along PLS axes you can use the shape.predictor function in geomorph.

In fact they provide a very good example in the help file for how to do this :) 


Here is an example of how to label points in a scatterplot.


plot(pls.object,pch = 21, col = "black",bg = "grey75", cex = 1)
text(pls.object$XScores[,1],pls.object$YScores[,1],labels = rownames(matrix_spe),cex = 0.7, offset = 2)
# matrix_spe, this object is a matrix that is used to define the second block.

Cheers,
Mohamad

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] PLS graphing help
parts:
Jessica,

Have you used picknplot.shape?  It allows you to make deformation grids for any point in the plot.

Also, plot.two.b.pls is an S3 generic plot function, meaning you can add stuff to your plot, just like any general R plot.  For example,

PLS <- two.b.pls(shape, mydata, …)
P <- plot(PLS, pch = 19, col = “yellow”)
text(x, y, mylabels, ...)

where mylabels is a vector of labels and x, y, are the coordinates where you want the labels to go.  You can find these in the P$plot.args, if they are the same locations as points.  Then, of course,

picknplot.shape(P, ...)

will allow you to generate deformation grids, if the data you used in PLS is appropriate (3D array rather than a matrix).

Good luck!
Mike
